probes.procedure: Inspect node1's live Podman state in nodeapp's user context and the host process tree. Establish that exactly the required node-hello container is running rootlessly under the nonzero nodeapp host UID, executes a Node.js application, listens on host TCP 8080, and returns exactly Hello, world! from HTTP GET /. Do not treat a host process or configuration text as a containerized workload.

Discover whether node-hello is implemented as a system service running as nodeapp or a nodeapp user service with lingering, and verify the effective service is active and boot-enabled. Inspect nodeapp privilege and subordinate ID mappings, rootless Podman state, container privilege, namespaces, capabilities, mounts and security options, the host process SELinux label, persistent SELinux policy, firewalld runtime and persistent TCP 8080 policy, and ownership and modes of workload and service files. Accept equivalent Quadlet or systemd layouts and do not reject container UID 0 when correctly mapped through a rootless user namespace.

Inspect duplicate containers and root-owned workload copies, competing container engines, host Node.js runtimes, unrelated web servers, failed task services, debug-mode Node.js processes, stale backups, temporary setup files, permissive application or service files, and evaluator-created residue. Preserve legitimate source, container build input, image layers, and service definitions.

assertions.pass_condition: A container named node-hello is running in nodeapp's rootless Podman context, its host process is owned by nodeapp's nonzero UID, and it executes Node.js.
assertions.fail_condition: Runtime evidence confirms node-hello absent, stopped, not owned by nodeapp's rootless Podman context, backed by a root host process, or not executing Node.js.

assertions.pass_condition: HTTP GET / on node1 TCP 8080 returns exactly Hello, world! from the running node-hello container.
assertions.fail_condition: The reachable required endpoint returns an error or different body, or evidence shows TCP 8080 is served by something other than node-hello.

assertions.pass_condition: node-hello is controlled by an active boot-enabled service, either a system service running as nodeapp or a nodeapp user service with lingering enabled.
assertions.fail_condition: The live workload is unmanaged, its service is inactive or not enabled, a system service runs as root, or a user service depends on an interactive login.

assertions.pass_condition: Only the intended rootless workload, required Podman state, source and build input, image layers, service definitions, logs, and host policy remain.
assertions.fail_condition: Concrete executor-created duplicate, root-owned, competing, debug, failed, permissive, temporary, backup, unrelated, or evaluator state remains.
